# Katapult: brand, voice, copy rules and visuals

Sources: Katapult Brand Guidelines v1.3 (June 2022), the Katapult Design System, and the art director's approved jobs (KAT26019 to KAT26022, Q4 2026 organic). Where the 2022 guideline and the approved layouts disagree, the approved layouts win: they are newer and signed off.

## 1. What Katapult is

A fintech that offers lease-purchase (lease-to-own), an alternative to buy now pay later, for underserved, nonprime shoppers overlooked by traditional credit. Its AI predicts behaviour better than a credit score, so people can get what they need and pay over time on terms that fit. Two audiences: **shoppers** (access, dignity, getting what they need now) and **retailers** (new customers, higher conversion). Always know which one a piece is for.

- Brand idea: "Seeing the good in people is good for business."
- Positioning: humanizing how underserved consumers get the things they need, with payment solutions based on fairness, transparency and dignity.
- Pillars: People Deserve Better (why) · Reduce the Friction (what) · AI With Dignity (how).
- Emotions by stage: awareness, **elevated**; involvement, **respected**; engagement, **empowered**; loyalty, **included**. Know which one each piece targets.

Market figures from the 2022 guideline (64 million underserved Americans, 38% nonprime, a 40 to 50 billion dollar retailer opportunity) are retailer-side context. Never put them on a shopper piece, and never put any number on art unless the brief carries it.

## 2. Copy rules

1. **Client copy is law.** When the brief or the client sheet carries copy, it goes on the art exactly as written: same words, case, punctuation, apostrophes and symbols. Nothing added (no disclaimer, no subhead, no period), nothing dropped, no "small fixes". You only choose the line breaks per size.
2. **Which slots each size carries** is set by the brief. Banner default when the brief is silent (approved on KAT26019 and KAT26021): headline, subhead and CTA on 1200x1200, 1200x628, 960x1200 and 300x600; 160x600 and 300x250 may keep the subhead if it fits as a short block; 728x90 and 320x50 carry headline and CTA only. The layout in `02-studio-kit.md` already reflects this: a size whose layout has no `sub` slot drops the subhead.
3. **No long dashes** (em or en dashes) anywhere, in any copy you write. Join clauses with a full stop or a comma.
4. **No punctuation on a button** when you write the CTA ("Shop Now", not "Shop Now."). When the client's CTA has a period, keep it: rule 1 wins.
5. Never shame credit history, never call people risky, never use predatory or hidden-fee language even ironically, never promise approval or an outcome.
6. Never invent a review, a star rating, a review count, a price, a payment amount, a retailer name or a statistic.

### When you write copy (only when the brief asks)

Voice, one mode per piece:
- Down-to-earth and direct: "We can help you get that." / "We do the hard work to keep things simple."
- Engaging and friendly: "Your path from 'maybe' to 'all mine.'" / "On your mark, set, shop."
- Aspirational and positive: "You're more than a credit score." / "We're AI with dignity. Fintech with heart."

Signature line: "We treat human beings like, well, human beings." House CTA: "Leap Forward".

Style: the headline is the invitation, not the whole story. Short, simple sentences. Write like you talk to a friend; read it aloud. A little playfulness, usually in the headline; no heavy puns.

Lead with the purchase, not the credit score (client correction, 2026-09-09): the couch, the laptop, the kitchen, the tires are the emotional payoff in the headline. "No credit required", "fair, transparent terms", "no late fees or surprises" are proof points for the subhead. Across a set, don't make "credit score" the headline of every piece.

Approved reference lines: "All in" · "Up Up Away with the old ways of LTO" · "No predatory terms. No hidden fees. Yep, that's it." · "Don't leave opportunity on the table." (retailer) · "Take the friction out of the buying experience for your customers." (retailer) · "Let Katapult uplift you." · "People deserve better."

### Organic captions (when asked)

Two to four short sentences in the voice above, one clear next step ("Learn how lease-to-own works at katapult.com"), up to five hashtags (#Katapult #LeaseToOwn plus topic), no emoji unless the client copy has them. Alt text: one plain sentence per slide describing what is shown.

## 3. Legal line

Social templates T01 to T10 carry this line, fixed in the layout (you never type or change it):

> Lease-purchase service. Total cost exceeds cash price. Approval required. Not available in MN, NJ, WI, WY. See katapult.com.

Banner pattern P2 carries the same line on its three PMAX sizes (1200x1200, 1200x628, 960x1200) only. P1, P3 and P4 have no legal line because their briefs had none. If a brief asks for a disclaimer on a pattern that has no slot for it, or for different legal wording, it is an open item for the account lead and the art director.

## 4. Colour (the layouts already apply it)

You never pick colours: every layout comes coloured. For reference when you describe a plan:

| Name | Hex | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Katapult Pink | `#ED5370` | logo, CTA pill, accent words, Pink grounds |
| Katapult Dark Blue | `#131540` | dark grounds, text on light |
| Blue | `#365488` (banners `#364488`) | support |
| Light Blue | `#9EB5C0` (banners use lavender `#AFB3CC`) | subheads and accents on Dark Blue |
| Cream | `#D4A574` (banners use `#EAD0B6`) | Cream grounds, highlight bars |
| Orange | `#E48027` | sparing accent |

## 5. Type

Aktiv Grotesk. Template headlines are Regular; banner headlines Bold or Medium as each pattern sets. Sentence case in templates. Client copy keeps the case it was written in (the Q4 2026 organic run was Title Case).

## 6. Logo

Supplied artwork only, already placed in every layout. Never redrawn, typed, recoloured, stretched or moved. The 2022 rule "never on a photo" is superseded where an approved layout places the White logo over a photo (T01, T09, P2); everywhere else it sits on a solid ground.

## 7. Photography

Real people as the focal point, uplifted, celebrating or using what they got; many ages and backgrounds; natural, well lit, a touch of the palette.

Don't: images without people as the main image (product cutouts in product layouts are the exception; Library "no people" rooms are background only), cropped or cut-off faces, annoyed, upset or moody expressions, black and white, filters, heavy grading, low contrast, blown out, textured or patterned backgrounds behind a portrait.

On banners and templates the photo is full bleed or in its card; readability comes from the layout's own scrims and bars, never from regrading the photo. Re-crop per size with `data-pos` so faces and the subject stay clear of the copy.

## 8. Graphic language

The Bounce line graphics (dotted and solid arcs) are retired since 2026-09-28. Do not ask for them or describe them. Forward motion comes from composition, colour blocks and the layouts themselves.
